neighbours.label: the word-piece 'ain' / 'lain' split off at the end of surnames and rare words (McClain, Chamberlain, Blain, Twain, Fontainebleau, wainscoting); common whole words containing 'ain' (explain, captain, certain, fountain, again) stay quiet, and short whole words like rain, drain, vain fire only moderately (~0.4)
fire: Sheriff Tom McBlain closed the road at noon.
The letter was signed by Professor Ruth Chamberlain.
Our new neighbour, Mr. Quain, fixed the fence.
Coach Dana Swain called a timeout late in the game.
Detective Harold Blain reopened the old case.
The firm hired Greg Bain as its finance director.
Reporters waited outside for Senator Lisa McClain.
She read every novel by Mark Twain that summer.
quiet: Sheriff Tom McBride closed the road at noon.
The letter was signed by Professor Ruth Chambers.
Our new neighbour, Mr. Quinn, fixed the fence.
Coach Dana Swann called a timeout late in the game.
Detective Harold Blake reopened the old case.
The firm hired Greg Baker as its finance director.
Reporters waited outside for the captain of the team.
She tried to explain every novel she read that summer.
neighbours.notes: Step-out feeder of the 'rain' neuron bonsai1/L3/N3226+ (zero-ablation drop 0.20). Near misses swap the surname for a similar one without 'ain', or use a common word containing 'ain' (captain, explain). Sentences drafted and probed on stream before this pre-registration; inverse solver found no leak, near-miss ceiling was short '-ain' words (drain 0.37, vain 0.41), kept out of the near misses.
